Give readable names to clusters

Source: R/name_clusters.R
name_clusters.Rd

A cluster identifier ("01", "cl_12") says nothing about its content. name_clusters() gives each cluster a provisional label that helps reading plots and tables, with one of three methods: the words that distinguish the cluster from the others ("tf-idf"), or the metadata of its most central node ("tidygraph_functions") or of its node with the highest value of a given column ("given_column"). These labels are starting points for interpretation, not the result of it: naming a cluster requires reading its documents, the references they share, and what distinguishes them from neighbouring clusters (Ding 2011) .

Usage

name_clusters(
  graphs,
  method = c("tidygraph_functions", "given_column", "tf-idf"),
  name_dynamic_clusters = FALSE,
  cluster_id,
  label_columns,
  label_name = "cluster_label",
  tidygraph_function = NULL,
  order_by = NULL,
  text_columns = NULL,
  nb_terms_label = 3,
  name_merged_clusters = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

graphs

A tbl_graph or a list of tbl_graphs.

method

"tf-idf" (chosen when no method is given), "tidygraph_functions" or "given_column" (see the details).

name_dynamic_clusters

Logical. TRUE when cluster_id identifies clusters across a list of graphs (the dynamic clusters of merge_dynamic_clusters()): each cluster then gets one name, computed on all its nodes in all windows. FALSE (default) names the clusters of each graph separately.

cluster_id

Character scalar, the node column with the clusters to name.

label_columns

For "tidygraph_functions" and "given_column", the node column(s) used to build the label of the chosen node, joined by "_" (e.g. c("source_author", "source_year")).

label_name

Character scalar, the name of the new column ("cluster_label" by default).

tidygraph_function

For "tidygraph_functions", a call to a centrality function of tidygraph, such as tidygraph::centrality_pagerank() (see tidygraph::centrality).

order_by

For "given_column", the numeric node column used to choose the node (e.g. "node_size" from build_network() with compute_size = TRUE, i.e. the most cited document of the cluster).

text_columns

For "tf-idf", the node column(s) with text (titles, abstracts, keywords), passed to extract_tfidf().

nb_terms_label

For "tf-idf", the number of terms in each label (3 by default), separated by commas. A term that is part of a term already in the label, or contains one, is skipped ("business" after "business cycle").

name_merged_clusters

Former name of name_dynamic_clusters.

...

For "tf-idf", other arguments of extract_tfidf() (e.g. clean_word_method, n_gram, ngrams_filter).

Value

The same object as graphs, with a new node column label_name, also joined to the edges through their cluster column.

Details

tf-idf. Each cluster is treated as one document made of the texts of its nodes, and each term \(t\) (word or n-gram) gets the weight $$\mathrm{tf}_{tc} \times \mathrm{idf}_t = \frac{n_{tc}}{\sum_u n_{uc}} \times \log\frac{C}{\mathrm{df}_t}$$ (Spärck Jones 1972; Salton and Buckley 1988) , with \(n_{tc}\) the number of occurrences of \(t\) in cluster \(c\), \(C\) the number of clusters and \(\mathrm{df}_t\) the number of clusters where \(t\) appears. The label gathers the terms with the highest weight: frequent in the cluster, rare in the others. With name_dynamic_clusters = FALSE, the comparison is made within each graph, so clusters of different windows may get the same label.

Most central node. "tidygraph_functions" computes the centrality given in tidygraph_function on each graph (it is added as a node column) and labels each cluster with the node with the highest value. The centrality is computed on the whole graph, not within the cluster. This method needs a network structure and therefore cannot be used with name_dynamic_clusters = TRUE.

Given column. "given_column" labels each cluster with its node with the highest order_by value: for an article network, typically its most cited article.

Nodes of an unnamed cluster get "no_name".

References

Ding Y (2011). “Community Detection: Topological vs. Topical.” Journal of Informetrics, 5(4), 498–514. doi:10.1016/j.joi.2011.02.006 .

Salton G, Buckley C (1988). “Term-Weighting Approaches in Automatic Text Retrieval.” Information Processing & Management, 24(5), 513–523.

Spärck Jones K (1972). “A Statistical Interpretation of Term Specificity and Its Application in Retrieval.” Journal of Documentation, 28(1), 11–21.

See also

extract_tfidf() to see more terms than the labels show.

Examples

network <- build_network(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  method = "similarity",
  edges_threshold = 1
)
#> ℹ Coupling (`biblionetwork::biblio_coupling()`) with "similarity": ties
#>   weighted by the idf-weighted cosine of the two lists of targets, after Shen
#>   et al. (2019), between source_id entities sharing target_id entities.
#> ℹ Two source_id are linked when they share at least 1 target_id
#>   (`edges_threshold`).
#> ℹ Nodes without any edge are removed (`keep_singleton = FALSE`).
network <- add_clusters(
  network,
  clustering_method = "leiden",
  objective_function = "modularity",
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# The words of the titles that distinguish each cluster
network <- name_clusters(
  network,
  method = "tf-idf",
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  text_columns = "source_title",
  nb_terms_label = 3,
  clean_word_method = "none"
)

# The article with the highest PageRank of each cluster
network <- name_clusters(
  network,
  method = "tidygraph_functions",
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  label_columns = c("source_author", "source_year"),
  label_name = "central_article",
  tidygraph_function = tidygraph::centrality_pagerank()
)
unique(tidygraph::as_tibble(network, active = "nodes")[
  c("cluster_leiden", "cluster_label", "central_article")
])
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   cluster_leiden cluster_label                            central_article
#>   <chr>          <chr>                                    <chr>          
#> 1 02             great inflation, stabilization, monetary VELDE-F_2004   
#> 2 01             productivity, unemployment, prices       WACHTER-M_1978 
#> 3 04             stagflation, inflation, 1970s            DELONG-B_1997  
#> 4 03             oil, great stagflation, price shocks     BARSKY-R_2002
